verdict.tagline: Charming anime aesthetics clash brilliantly with psychological horror.
for_you_if: you enjoy psychological horror mixed with minigames
you want a compact narrative adventure completed in one sitting
you appreciate detailed anime-inspired visual styles
not_for_you_if: you dislike sudden jump scares or gore
you want deep action rather than puzzles

cohorts.summary: Reviewers praise the engaging mix of minigames, puzzles, and psychological horror wrapped in a detailed anime art style, noting smooth performance and a short completion time.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes jump scares, while also providing an option to blur gore for sensitive players.

citations.review_text: Definitely a game I would recommend to people who dream of being sucked into a video game. However, some parts do contain jump scares. If you are squeamish, there is an option to turn on blurring of any g*re, which is nice. However, it's a shame the MiSide x DDLC collab got cancelled. Good game otherwise.

This game really surprised me! A lot scarier than I thought it was going to be. Interesting story and fun gameplay even if the puzzles were on the easier side. Perfect length for what it is! A nice little gem of a game :)

ps. has a couple of jump scares, in case you are sensitive to them

claims.claim: This cohort describes the gameplay as incorporating various mini-games and puzzles between walking simulator and narrative segments.

citations.review_text: Overall one of the best games I've played, I loved the storyline itself but the mini games collectables and puzzles are super fun too.

Mild spoilers ahead.

This game is... Fantastic! While the runtime isn't especially long, the game has quite a bit of character. While horror makes up a good chunk of the game, I personally found it more comedic than scary. Still, there were a couple of moments that actually got a jump out of me.

The main reason I really like this game is Mita herself, as well as all of her variations. Despite technically being the same characters, they all somehow are completely unique. I find her critiques about how our world operates to be very relatable and grounded, even if it isn't exactly profound stuff on its own. The execution is what really makes it work. The writing is very good; so much so that I'd go as far as to say Mita is the best written Yandere I've ever seen. She's somehow both very sympathetic and terrifying at the same time. Truthfully, I felt bad for her despite her otherwise horrible actions during the story. I wanted to see her destroyed, but also interested in seeing if she had any motivations beyond wanton destruction. I was pleased to find out that both conclusions were handled in a satisfying way!

As far as gameplay goes, expect basic puzzling, minigames, and lots of walking. The main draw for this game is character dialogue and interactions.

I unlocked Peaceful Mode which, at the time of writing, hasn't actually been implemented yet. I will be eagerly awaiting the chance to experience something akin to a Life Sim game with Mita. I'm sure she would be just as thrilled.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game runs well without experiencing frame drops, lag, or technical issues on Steam.

citations.review_text: game is great on steam, no issues.

Awesome game, actually jumped at some parts, and overall just really well made and polished, with no frame drops or lag that I encountered. Absolutely great experience. I recommend playing with the Russian VO, as the voice actors did a pretty nice job with it.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that character dialogue and interactions are a primary focus of the experience.

citations.review_text:
[h1]True evolution of Visual Novel genre in 202x[/h1]

Yes, MiSide is short. Sometimes the mood does not quite land, and a few assets feel strange. BUT:

* Cute girls
* Optional activities
* Short, sharp, on-point dialogue
* 3D subtitles - seriously, wow
* Just enough interactivity to keep you engaged

Do not judge it purely by whether you like Mita, the setting, or the story.

Look at what the developers actually achieved: they gave the visual novel genre a fresh identity, modern presentation, and a level of interactivity most VNs never even attempt.

[b]The true successor to DDLC? Honestly, it might be.[/b]

Mild spoilers ahead.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features minigames and puzzles alongside its walking simulator elements to break up the gameplay.

citations.review_text:
Big, big fan of this meta narrative. While it wasn't nearly as scary or "psychologically damaging" as the hype I've seen surrounding it lead me to expect, MiSide is massively clever and a fairly engrossing story if I'm being honest. 

It's actually a perfect length for this type of game. Mostly walking sim with some simple yet fun puzzles and mini games to break it up. Enough variation across its 19 chapters to keep it interesting and full of so many "oh that's neat" surprises. 

A good time! Honestly the upsetting thing about this game is the blank look of disappointment Mita gives you when you manage to click the "exit" button in the main menu.
This game is amazing! I love the puzzles and minigames, and Cappie is really entertaining. I totally recommend this game

This game is a clever, creepy and surprisingly fun experience. The game constantly changes things up with puzzles, minigames and different versions of the same world, so it never feels repetitive. I loved the little environmental details, the different Mitas, and how the story slowly becomes more disturbing and philosophical. It also plays with ideas and makes references to other psychological horror games, while still creating its own identity. I enjoyed it enough to immediately play it again for another ending. Definitely worth experiencing blind.

Mild spoilers ahead.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring an art style with detailed 3D models and character animations.

citations.review_text:
Absolutely beautiful art-style and incredibly expressive and alive models and voice actors. Seriously A+ on all presentation. This game looks, sounds and controls fantastic.

The story however is laughably predictable, and the moment to moment gameplay is where MiSide really struggles. None of the horror elements are remotely scary, there's no build up of atmosphere or tension at any point and the monsters are generic and uninspired, usually some different form of Mita. Horror gameplay is nothing you haven't seen 1000 times before: mannequins that only move when you look away, quick time event chase sequences, random glitch effects and abrupt jumpscares. Really a shame the gameplay is so generic considering how unique and impressive the visuals are. 

You can upskirt the hot anime girl in camera mode though so take my criticisms with a grain of salt.

Concept 10/10
3D models 10/10
Animations 10/10
SFX/OST 10/10

Quite an achievement for a couple of people…a fun first-person game with occasional horror elements.

I bought this after reading about a list of games of the year about how this was a great psychological horror game…and yet all of the marketing makes it look like a cute mobile dating sim. I’m a fan of psychological thrillers, so I figured a slight shift over to the psychological horror genre wouldn’t be a big deal. I played it through in one long sitting, and it’s a beautiful game and an amazing feat for such a small team. While you have to like the kind of game that jumps between video game genres (think: Evoland) and is story-driven (in 3D form, the adventure game type known as “walking simulators”) for this to appeal to you, it is fun. It’s not very difficult unless you go for the achievements (in which case it’s moderately difficult), and it is unique.

The Positives:
-The art design of the Mitas is amazing. It feels like interacting with a Japanese Anime character. I couldn’t stop admiring the animation.

-As with TV’s “bottle episodes”, this game gets creative with what you can do in a limited world. They find ways to change the environment without requiring the game to have 35 levels like more epic-type games would do.

-I enjoyed the voice acting, the environments, and the story. It was worth playing for the experience.

-If you don’t love the horror genre, you can still play this as long as you can handle some creepiness.  I estimated around 5 jump scares, and they weren’t too bad. The worst scare-wise was how they could make the cutest animated character creepy in many different ways. So, I think that folks who avoid Resident Evil-like games for their horror elements could do this game just fine—it’s more weird and freaky than horror scary for all but a few instances.


The Negatives:
-Instead of creating a lot of gameplay and environments in the world, they went the way of making almost a dozen mini-games within the game to play. While each was fun, you …

Probably one of the only games I actually got scared in while playing. Went in completely blind and ended up finishing the whole game in one sitting, I never thought it could be this engaging. Atmosphere is great, character models are amazing, and it genuinely had me jumping during some of the sections. Definitely worth picking up if you have the time for it (which you should considering it barely takes 4 hours to beat the game) and I would say its even worth replaying for the 100%.

Peaceful mode never lol

I loved this game so much. the art style alone deserves a good review, its so beautiful and polished. the story was so well delivered/paced and did so well on the psychological horror front. 

play this game if u wanna larp a woman being interested in you

this game is so cool, it has actually scary moments and liminal feels, other parts are very cozy and silly

I came into this game blind. I barely played the demo because I did not want to ruin anything and I am very glad I did it that way, because HOLY HELL. It starts out a little slow and ill admit a bit boring, but do not give up! I promise it is totally worth it! I have a high scare tolerance so I wouldnt say this game is terribly scary (besides that one jump scare, ♥♥♥♥ you Mita) but it gave me an uncomfortable feeling the whole time. Every time you think the game is over... surprise, it's not and keeps you hanging on. I also loved how it wasn't easy to predict what was coming next and that's something that I don't see in these types of games nowadays. As someone who LOVES DDLC, I can see some inspiration taken from that game and used here in its own style. Im not sure who is crazier, Monica or Crazy Mita. I will be 100% this game. I will also tell my friends its an innocent dating/life sim.

Miside is one of these short games that you will keep in mind for a pretty long time while watching a lot of videos about easter eggs, the lore and the theories that you'll find interesting. There is just a few jumpscares and it's perfect, I hate when games just use jumpscares for nothing, in this game, it’s well done and designed to really give us a fright at the time, but the real scary part is all the atmosphere that is really immersive.

I highly recommend it if you want a fun evening with a good game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features minigames, quick-time events, chase sequences, and hidden object segments.

citations.review_text:
I'm sure this game works for some people. I think I'm just not the target demographic. I'm jaded. The storyline feels kind of obvious and unsurprising, like something for r/im14andthisisdeep. The [spoiler]yandere[/spoiler] thing isn't new to me at all, even if it's in a slightly different shape this time. But mostly I just don't like the actual gameplay. It's all just dumb minigames, QTEs, annoying chases, frustrating hidden object segments, and too much repetition for my tastes. I also never felt like anything I did mattered. It was all basically a kinetic novel with annoying minigames gating progress. Even if I felt for a certain Mita and actually wanted to stay and be her companion, I knew she was just going to get left behind [spoiler]or even killed[/spoiler] and there was no way I could choose otherwise, because the game said I couldn't. I didn't like the feeling that I had no agency.

Sorry, it's a reasonably-well-made game, and I do like the art direction (though I think there's something broken about the lighting and I wish I could talk to whoever set up the shaders in this game, because I can't think it's deliberate), and the idea was decent, I just don't like the actual game that I played and I feel like it wasn't a good use of my time. I'd probably give it a neutral if I could, but I definitely wouldn't give it a positive.

Pretty cool game, lots of easter eggs and side-contents along the way. I like how it allows players to immerse with the characters despite the limited time we spend with them jumping between versions. Each characters are unique and are chill to spend time with. I'd recommend the game if you're looking for a blend of horror and interactive, funny & emotional moments with the characters. The minigames are not that difficult, yet fun.

One thing I'd probably criticize is that it probably needs more content with other characters, as in more interactions/minigames/dialogues. Would be pretty cool if they add more difficulties that'd test more of our capabilities in the future, since they'll be adding more endings maybe additional challenges in each chapters? Nevertheless, it's a fun game!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes multiple endings and collectibles, adding replayability.

citations.review_text:
This is one of the best horror games that I've ever played HANDS DOWN; it is not to be sat on. I love this new concept, but I will not spoil anything for any potential readers, and I highly recommend just turning your lights off, locking yourself into a room, and going into this game blind at 3:00am. *Also*, you can learn about how love works!

Yeah sure, it's short for the money, okay? I get it. (It took me around six and a half hours for a full enjoyment run--I still missed a lot of collectibles, and there are a few different endings which also add to re-playability, as well as the new Peaceful mode which others seem to be enjoying!) If you aren't into anime, it may *not* be of interest to you. But if you don't mind that part (or maybe even enjoy it), and you are an avid horror enthusiast, this is one for the books... 

I have played 50+ horror games in my lifetime and this one comes so close to my Top 5 that it took me off guard a bit with all of the pink. Hats off to AIHASTO, and please keep this up! 10/10

A cool, lovable, and delightfully random trip about obsession, cuteness, and psychological spookiness. Honestly, MiSide is a reality-bending ride that basically everyone should take once, not only weebs. It masterfully traps you inside a house with a cute but terrifyingly obsessed virtual girl named Mita. One of the coolest features is that you can use voice-dubs from passionate fans for nearly every language with one click right from the main menu. As you might have guessed by the look, it’s super economic also for older systems; it offers limited replayability mostly for collectibles and something new that will be added soon as they say, making it an absolute must-play.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the visual presentation as a blend of cute anime-inspired aesthetics and psychological horror elements.

citations.review_text:
ive had this game since 2024 (with a pirated version) and i can def say If you're looking for a AMAZING psychological horror game that's genuinely unique, I can't recommend MiSide enough. It starts off looking cute and lighthearted, but the atmosphere slowly shifts into something incredibly unsettling. The contrast between the charming visuals and the disturbing story is what makes it so memorable, constantly keeping you guessing about what's coming next.

One of the things I appreciated most was how well the game builds suspense without relying on cheap jump scares every few minutes. Instead, it creates a feeling of tension through its storytelling, sound design, and subtle environmental changes. Every new area feels like it has something to hide, making exploration exciting and nerve-racking at the same time.

The story is engaging from beginning to end, with plenty of twists that caught me completely off guard. The characters are surprisingly well-developed, and it's easy to become invested in what happens to them. The voice acting, music, and overall presentation all work together to create an immersive experience that draws you deeper into the game's world.

Visually, MiSide does an amazing job blending its cute anime-inspired aesthetic with psychological horror. That contrast is one of the game's biggest strengths, making the creepy moments hit even harder. The soundtrack deserves special praise as well—it knows exactly when to be calm, eerie, or intense, adding so much to the atmosphere.

I also enjoyed the puzzles and exploration. They never felt overly frustrating, and they fit naturally into the story instead of slowing the pace down. There are plenty of small details hidden throughout the game that reward players who take the time to look around, making repeat playthroughs worthwhile.

Overall, MiSide is one of the most memorable psychological horror games I've played. It's creative, emotionally engaging, and manages to keep you thinking long af…
